title: The Filtering Effects of Urban Environments on Frugivorous Birds Worldwide
content:
ABSTRACT

Aim

Frugivorous birds are highly susceptible to environmental changes caused by urbanization. However, little is known about the global consequences. Here, we examine global patterns of urban frugivorous bird diversity and the mechanisms driving these patterns.

Location

Global, across 1414 urban areas.

Time Period

Contemporary.

Major Taxa Studied

Frugivorous birds.

Methods

After compiling a global dataset of urban bird assemblages, we compared the species richness and composition of frugivorous birds in urban areas with those of their regional species pools derived from BirdLife range maps and partitioned the composition dissimilarity into its spatial turnover and nestedness components. We assessed how climatic, ecological, socio-economic, and biogeographic factors accounted for variation in the species richness of urban frugivorous birds.

Results

We identified 557 frugivorous bird species in these urban areas. Variations in the species richness among urban areas were significantly associated with temperature, historical biogeography, habitat heterogeneity, socio-economic conditions, and the diversity of fleshy-fruited trees. Globally, the total number of frugivorous bird species in urban areas was 33.9% lower than in the combined regional species pools. Individually, 531 urban areas exhibited lower frugivorous richness, 329 matched their regional levels, and 554 had higher frugivorous richness than their regional species pools. These declines were more pervasive in tropical regions, where ca. 91.8% of urban areas contained fewer frugivorous species. The compositional dissimilarity between urban assemblages and their regional species pools was dominated by nestedness, regardless of whether the urban areas gained or lost species.

Main Conclusions

Our results highlight the strong filtering effects of urbanization on frugivorous birds. These insights can inform strategies for conserving frugivores in cities.
